title: Clip a binder clip onto a stack of paper: squeeze its handles, slide it over the edge, let go, fold the handles down
instruction: Clip the stack of paper standing in the letter sorter with the binder clip on the desk: squeeze its two handles to open it, slide it down over the stack's top edge near the right corner as far as it goes, let go, then fold both handles down flat against the paper.
context: Binder clips hold loose papers together in every office and school bag. This is the opposite act to the merged task remove-binder-clip-before-shredding, which takes a binder clip off a stack: here the clip goes on. Its steel jaw is a strong spring that opens only while the two wire handles are squeezed together. The open jaw is slid over the stack's edge until the paper reaches the back of the jaw, then let go so it springs shut on the paper, and each handle is folded down flat so the bundle can be filed. Squeezed too little, the lips stop on the edge; let go too early, they bite a few millimetres and the clip slips off; pushed carelessly, the stack is shoved off its wall. Squeezed all the way until the handles stand parallel, the clip twists in the fingers and one side snaps shut. Here the 40 sheets stand in a desk letter sorter, so one hand holds the stack while the other works the clip.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. A small three-slot metal mesh letter sorter (178 long, 83 deep, 133 tall; walls 60, 85, 110 and 133 tall front to back, 24 mm slots, estimates) stands at x 185-268, y -80 to +98, slots running left to right. A stack of 40 sheets of 80 g/m2 A5 copy paper (210 x 148, 4.0 thick, 100 g) stands on its long edge in the front slot, foot against the front wall, leaning back 13.5 degrees on the first divider, y -130 to +80 (right end 50 past the sorter), top edge 147 high. A medium binder clip (32 wide, 16 capacity; black spring-steel body, jaw 19.5 deep; two silver 1.4 mm wire handles, loops 37 long; about 8 g; estimates except width and capacity) stands on its closed jaws at x 150, y -165, jaw line along y, both handles up. Its spring (estimate): lips 3 N together when empty, about 7 N on the 4 mm stack, about 17 N at the handle ends to hold the lips 9.5 mm apart, about 25 N to open it fully.
scoring: Judged once both grippers are at least 30 mm from the clip and the paper and neither has moved more than 1 mm for 1 s. Score 0 if the clip is not on the stack (the paper's top edge less than 3 mm into the jaw, the lips less than 2.5 mm apart, either clip end less than 3 mm inside the paper's ends, or the clip on the table), or the stack is out of place (its foot more than 10 mm off the slot floor, or the stack more than 10 mm off the front wall or off the divider it leans on); otherwise the lowest of: seat, paper's top edge to the back of the jaw (1.0 within 3 mm, 0.75 within 6 mm, 0.5 within 12 mm, else 0.25); square, the lip line against the top edge (1.0 within 3 degrees, 0.75 within 8, else 0.5); stack against the wall and divider (1.0 within 2 mm, 0.75 within 5 mm, else 0.5); handles folded down, loop end 20 mm or more below the lips and within 10 mm of the paper (1.0 both, 0.75 one, 0.5 none).
reset_notes: Take the clip off, tap the 40 sheets square on the desk, stand them back in the sorter's front slot on their long edge, foot against the front wall, right end 50 mm past the sorter, leaning on the first divider, and stand the clip on its closed jaws at its mark with both handles up. About one minute.
fidelity: GPU PhysX 240 Hz. The 40 sheets are one rigid 4 mm block: single sheets, their bending and slip are not modelled. Clip: published width and capacity; other sizes, spring, handle friction, masses and frictions are estimates. Jaw walls hinge at the spine corners on torsion springs; handles turn in the rolled lips. Solver settings only: 64 position iterations, jaw-hinge inertia and damping. Sorter panels are solid plates. The demo reads object poses; nothing is attached or teleported.
